scripts.//build: Declarations only — see tsconfig.build.json. wrangler builds the worker itself; this exists so apps/editor can infer its API client from AppType without compiling the worker's source.
scripts.//build:skill-index: Crawls the allowlisted skills repositories and writes the index to the file named as its argument. Deliberately NOT part of `build` or `deploy`: it reaches the live GitHub API and the thing it produces is published to KV by .github/workflows/build-skill-index.yml, not by a deploy. Takes GITHUB_TOKEN if one is set and runs unauthenticated if not, so it can be run by hand.
scripts.//db:generate: The write path and the gate for migrations/, which is generated output that had neither. Edit src/db/*.schema.ts, run `db:generate`, commit the .sql file and the snapshot beside it; `db:generate:check` is the same run against a throwaway copy, reporting what it would have written and writing nothing. The check runs in CI's check job, as a turbo task, and on the pre-commit hook under the same `...[HEAD]` filter as lint and test. It is needed because a worker ships code and not schema: an index, a `notNull`, a unique constraint or a foreign key added to the schema type-checks, lints and passes the whole suite — the suite applies the COMMITTED migrations, so the tables the tests use are the old ones — and the first sign of the missing migration is `wrangler d1 migrations apply` at deploy time putting code at the edge that expects a column nothing ever added. Unlike the vendored trees in packages/cli this one cannot be regenerated from scratch and compared: drizzle-kit diffs against the snapshot in migrations/meta/, so from scratch everything looks new. scripts/check-migrations.ts says how regenerating on top of a copy answers the same question, and why the verdict is read off drizzle-kit's own words rather than its exit code.
